text: 🏘️🇲🇽 514,000 new homes already approved — 43% of Infonavit's six-year goal. "Of the 1.2 million homes the institute has set as its goal, 440 housing developments are already approved — that's 514,000 new homes, a 43 percent advance on the six-year target." — Octavio Romero Oropeza, Infonavit director, in Cuautla Vivienda para el Bienestar aims to build 1.8 million homes for workers earning one to two minimum wages, deliver 1 million property titles, and restructure unpayable credits for 5 million families. Today in Cuautla: 128 new homes and 207 titles delivered.

"We're going to build together, because this is everyone's work — families caring for their children, the state government, the federal government. And together, we will build peace and justice in this wonderful municipality." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, in Cuautla, Morelos Two months after Cuautla's mayor was arrested on organized-crime charges, Sheinbaum arrived with a federal reinforcement: house-by-house attention starting next week, 10 new public high schools, youth jobs through Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro, and more National Guard presence. text:
🇲🇽🏭 <u>EVERY MEXICAN JOB CREATES TWO IN THE US: SHEINBAUM</u>

Mexico doesn't take jobs from the United States — it multiplies them. "It's proven that one job in Mexico represents at least two jobs in the United States," President Sheinbaum said Friday, as the T-MEC review advances and Washington's protectionists push to reshore plants north of the border, El Economista reports. Production crosses the border and back; employment grows on both sides.

🇲🇽🛡️ <u>PLAN MORELOS: HOMICIDES DOWN 54%</u>

Three months after the federal government launched Plan Morelos, the state is posting real numbers: intentional homicides down 54% between September 2024 and June 2026, vehicle theft down 32%, high-impact crime down 9% versus last year — and June 2026 was the least violent month since 2019. Federal, state and municipal coordination delivering what years of promises couldn't.

🇲🇽🌾 <u>HUNGER FALLS IN MEXICO AND LATIN AMERICA: FAO</u>

Global hunger fell for a third straight year — from 8.6% to 7.8% since 2022, 43 million fewer people — and Latin America leads the decline at 4.8%, below 2015 levels, per the UN's SOFI 2026 report. In Mexico and Central America hunger dropped from 5.7% to 5.1%, which the report attributes to employment recovery and inflation control, crediting targeted social protection, school meals and cash transfers for the region's results.
banner: FAO: HUNGER FALLS IN MEXICO, LATAM

text:
🇲🇽🌎 <u>SHEINBAUM CONFIRMS: NO NEW US TARIFFS ON MEXICO</u>

Mexico keeps exactly the trade terms it had a week ago, President Sheinbaum confirmed after meeting US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer: zero tariffs on everything shipped under T-MEC rules except vehicles and steel, 10% on the rest. "Mexico is exactly where we were a week ago; we don't have a new tariff," she said. The real fight comes next — Washington wants regional content hiked from 70% to 90%, and Mexico insists Mexican-made production counts, not just US-made.
banner: SHEINBAUM: NO NEW US TARIFFS ON MEXICO

text:
🇲🇽🎓 <u>UNAM FREEZES 2026 ENROLLMENTS AFTER EXAM FRAUD SCANDAL</u>

Mexico's UNAM suspended all new undergraduate enrollments for the 2026-2027 cycle — an unprecedented move — after TikTok tutorials on beating its AI-proctored admission exam went viral: second phones hidden in camera blind spots, earpieces under long hair, Discord screen-sharing. A technical commission convened by rector Leonardo Lomelí will review the entire selection process before any inscription resumes, to "safeguard certainty for all participants" and guarantee "integrity and academic honesty."
banner: UNAM SUSPENDS ENROLLMENT OVER EXAM FRAUD

text:
🚨🇲🇽 <u>FAR-RIGHT CONQUEST PARADE CANCELLED IN MEXICO CITY</u>

Organizers of the so-called Paseo del Pendón — a colonial-era parade glorifying the Spanish Conquest — called off their August 14-15 event after far-right groups piled onto the call, citing a "climate of polarization and intolerance." President Sheinbaum had already shrugged off the revival attempt: exalting Hernán Cortés didn't go well for them last time either. Five centuries on, the Conquest still has no parade in Mexico.

🇲🇽📊 <u>ENOE: MEXICO LOST 319,633 JOBS IN JUNE — THE STRUCTURAL CHALLENGE IN ONE NUMBER</u>

Hard data from INEGI, via El Economista: 319,633 jobs gone in June, the second worst month of 2026, leaving a half-year deficit of 293,227 — against the 1.2 million jobs a year Mexico needs just to absorb its growing workforce. Unemployment ticked up to 2.9% and informality still covers 55% of workers. This is exactly the gap that Plan México’s industrialization and formalization drive is built to close. The numbers don’t lie; neither does the task ahead.

🇲🇽🌳 <u>CERRO DE LA ESTRELLA: COMMUNITY RESTORATION TAKES ROOT IN IZTAPALAPA</u>

Mexico City’s environment secretariat is restoring one of the capital’s great urban lungs the old way — tequio, collective work. Over 100 volunteers have already planted 1,394 native trees of a planned 2,400: tepozán, huizache, cazahuate, palo dulce, chapulixtle. A specialized forest brigade, UAM Iztapalapa scientists and the Guardianes del Cerro neighborhood collective keep the hill under permanent watch. This is what public environmental policy looks like when the community owns it.
